_meta.description: VANILLA Morrowind crafting-process reference: how alchemy, enchanting, and armor repair work in the base game — constants parsed from the game ESMs (GMST records), process text quoted verbatim from the game's own help strings, formula structure from the community-documented engine (OpenMW reimplementation). Purpose: the baseline to diff NP's modified processes against as they are documented. NOTHING here is guaranteed to hold on NP — see each section's np_status.

s-gmst.note: GMST game-settings records parsed from the ESMs — the engine's actual tuning constants.

s-help.note: Verbatim in-game help/UI strings shipped in the ESMs.

s-engine.note: Formula structure per the OpenMW engine reimplementation (community-verified against vanilla behavior). Constants themselves come from s-gmst.

alchemy.summary: Potions are brewed from 2+ ingredients that share at least one effect, using apparatus (Mortar & Pestle required; Alembic, Calcinator, and Retort optionally modify quality). Skill and INT/LUK drive success and potion strength.

process.step: Effect visibility: an ingredient's effects are revealed in listed order as Alchemy skill rises — thresholds at fWortChanceValue x1/x2/x3/x4 (15/30/45/60 skill for effects 1-4).

Brewing requires a Mortar & Pestle; a shared effect between ingredients is what ends up in the potion. Alembic/Calcinator/Retort quality modifies the result (calcinator boosts, alembic reduces negative effects, retort boosts positives).

Potion strength scales with Alchemy skill + INT/10 + LUK/10, apparatus quality, and fPotionStrengthMult; resulting magnitude/duration scale via fPotionT1MagMult / fPotionT1DurMult, with fPotionMinUsefulDuration as the floor.

alchemy.np_status: NP modifications expected but not yet documented (see open_questions q:np-process-deltas). NP-side known so far: custom ingredients exist (alchemy.json np_ingredients).

enchanting.summary: Items are enchanted using a filled soul gem; the soul's charge becomes the item's charge pool, and the item type caps total enchantment cost. Self-enchanting success is skill-gated; constant effects need large souls.

strings: Slot for item to enchant. Only weapons, armor, scrolls and clothing that are not already enchanted can be enchanted.
Slot for the soul gem used to enchant an item. Only soul gems filled with a soul can be used. The soul amount is the total charge placed into the item.
The first number is the total amount the enchantment would cost to cast. The second number is the total enchantment cost that can be placed on this type of item.
The amount of charge points needed each time this enchantment is cast. This number is modified by your enchant skill.
The amount of soul in the soul gem in the soul gem slot
Type of cast for the enchantment.
Magic effects you know that you can add to an item

process.step: Only unenchanted weapons, armor, scrolls, and clothing can be enchanted; each item type has an enchant-point capacity that caps total enchantment cost (see vanilla_ref.json enchant_capacity per item).
A constant-effect enchantment requires a soul of at least iSoulAmountForConstantEffect (400) — in vanilla, Golden Saint / Ascended Sleeper tier.

Self-enchant success chance scales with Enchant skill (+INT/LUK contributions) against enchantment cost via fEnchantmentChanceMult (x3 on cost), halved again for constant effects (fEnchantmentConstantChanceMult 0.5) — large enchantments are near-impossible to self-make in vanilla.

Cast cost per use is reduced by Enchant skill (fEnchantmentMult 0.1 scaling); items recharge over time and from soul gems; enchanter NPCs charge fEnchantmentValueMult (1000) x enchantment cost in gold.

enchanting.np_status: NP HEAVILY modifies enchanting — the NP-side system (self-enchant ceilings, EV, the Infusion Anvil) is documented in data/enchanting.json; use THAT for NP answers. This section is the vanilla baseline only. Known deltas already: NP self-enchant ceilings are empirical per-slot caps unlike vanilla's chance-gated system; systematic diff pending (q:np-process-deltas).

repair.summary: Armor and weapons lose condition with use; repairing uses hammers/prongs consumed per attempt, with success and repair amount driven by Armorer skill.

process.step: Each repair attempt consumes one use of a repair item (Repair Prongs / hammers of increasing quality); success chance scales with Armorer skill (+STR? engine details), fatigue state, and luck; repaired amount scales with skill and tool quality via fRepairAmountMult (3).
NPC smiths offer paid repair (sServiceRepairTitle UI); items cannot be repaired above full condition in vanilla.

repair.np_status: NP modifications expected but not yet documented — NP items reach conditions far above vanilla norms (e.g. 6400/6400) and the Infusion Anvil adds +2250 durability, suggesting a reworked durability economy. Systematic diff pending (q:np-process-deltas).
